crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Self-Driving Laboratories
children.blurb: Self-driving laboratories are research facilities where software plans experiments, robotic hardware runs them, and instruments measure the results, with the loop repeating without a person at every step.

children.name: Digital Twins for Experiments
children.blurb: Digital twins for experiments are software replicas of a physical experimental setup, kept in step with the real instrument through a stream of measurements.

children.name: Instrument and Sensor Data
children.blurb: Instrument and sensor data covers the readings produced by laboratory hardware, from spectrophotometers and chromatographs to temperature probes, pressure transducers and environmental monitors.

children.name: Optimising Lab Protocols
children.blurb: Optimising lab protocols covers the use of computational methods to improve the design, scheduling and execution of wet lab procedures.

children.name: Forecasting Lab Supplies
children.blurb: Forecasting lab supplies covers the prediction of when a laboratory will run out of consumables, reagents, and other stocked items, and how much of each will be needed over a coming period.

sections.body: Laboratory automation and simulation covers the machinery and software that run experiments with less human hands-on time, and the models that predict what those experiments will do before anyone touches a pipette. In practice, AI here schedules robotic liquid handlers, reads instrument output, adjusts parameters between runs, and flags when a result looks wrong. Self-driving labs close the loop, where a model proposes a condition, a robot runs it, and the result feeds the next proposal. Digital twins mirror a physical setup in software so a protocol can be tried many times before it is run for real. The work is operational rather than speculative, and it sits close to the bench.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Closed-loop systems work well for narrow tasks such as solubility screens, crystallisation trials and simple assay optimisation, where the search space is bounded and the readout is fast. They struggle when experiments take days, when a step needs a human hand, or when the measurement itself is noisy. Digital twins are only as good as the physical model behind them, and many biological systems resist clean equations. Instrument data is often locked in vendor formats, which limits how much can be reused across labs. Forecasting supplies is largely a logistics problem dressed in AI, and it depends on records that many labs keep badly. Nothing here replaces judgement about which question is worth asking.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Start with Self-Driving Laboratories for the full loop of robot, model and decision, which is the centre of this section. Digital Twins for Experiments takes the simulation side and explains how a virtual copy is built and validated against real runs. Instrument and Sensor Data deals with the raw signal underneath both, including calibration, formats and the mess of connecting hardware to software. Optimising Lab Protocols narrows to the search itself, how conditions are chosen and improved across rounds. Forecasting Lab Supplies steps back to the inventory and ordering layer that keeps a running lab stocked. Read together they cover the cycle from prediction to execution to resupply.
